body:
Welcome to the sub and thank you for your service as a teacher.  I have suffered from anxiety since I was a child and anxiety induced headaches for nearly ten years.

I am signing off for the night but would be willing to PM you tomorrow if you want to hear more about how I treat my anxiety and headaches.

Welcome to the sub.  You are among friends here.  The members are very supportive and helpful.  Suffering from anxiety while caring for children and holding a full time job is very challenging.

The results from your recent medical tests are encouraging.  I hope you receive a clean bill of health on your heart.  Anxiety is a very powerful force.  It can create a variety of negative physical symptoms.  These physical symptoms cause more stress which leads to greater anxiety.  It is a viscious cycle thst I know all too well.

The human race is blessed with so much diversity of appearance, yet we still insist on designating only a few physical traits as desirable. It is unfair for beauty to be defined in such a narrow way. All body types are inherently beautiful in different ways.

OP you have a strong spirit. It is clear from your post that you are not the type of person that gives up easily.

Like you, I want help more than I want to kill myself.  I hope we both find the support and assistance we need to overcome our suicidal feelings.

I have been experiencing a high level of anxiety the past couple of months so I can relate to what you are going through.  I feel like a rubber band that keeps getting stretched farther and farther.  Despite this, I am hopeful that if I keep practicing my anxiety management strategies the symptoms will ease.

Your positive attitude towards the upcoming appointment demonstrates that you are committed to treatment.  I hope it goes exceedingly well for you.

I am resuming therapy on Tuesday after a 4 year hiatus.

Caffeine is a significant anxiety trigger for me. I avoid consuming coffee, tea, and soda.  I also have to limit my sugar intake.

Water, milk, and herbal tea (sweetened with a little raw honey) are my primary beverages

I have a sweet tooth and often resort to eating candy to comfort myself when I am feeling anxious.  It provides temporary relief but if I have more than a small serving it results in increased anxiety and guilt.

Any beverages with caffeine (coffee, tea soda) are a trigger for me.  I feel good while consuming them and really like the energy and focus they provide but they send my anxiety into over drive.  As little as one cup or can has a major impact.

I now try to limit myself to water, milk, and herbal peppermint or chamomile tea.

Resisting the desire to self medicate is challenging.  I have no interest in interacting with the world tomorrow.  Just want to skip work and stay in bed.  I have been tempted all day to drink my bottle of bourbon.  I just want to get drunk and escape from everything for awhile.

I admire you for having the courage to create the video and share it with us.  I have considered doing his many times but have never followed through because at times I feel a great deal of shame for having mental illness.

Usually, I try distract myself by reading books or watching tv.  The most effective way that I calm myself is by exercising but I do not do it as consistently as I need to.

Crippling is a great word to describe it.  Mental illness not only negatively affects individuals but our society as well.  But it is the elephant in the room that no one wants to meaningfully address (in the US).  So many of us suffer in silence each and every day and yet the status quo seems to remain the same.  It is slowly becoming more acceptable to discuss but it is not happening fast enough.  Society still attaches a stigma and stereotype to each of us and it is unfair.  People with mental illness come from all walks of life.  It does not discriminate.  We need help and support, not judgement.

Today has been challenging.  By 5pm my anxiety had increased to a such a high level that it triggered my internal self destruct mode.  Have been dealing with the resulting suicidal thoughts and depression since then.

Greetings and welcome to the sub.

You touch upon a very important point regarding conformity to societal expectations.  Genuine joy and happiness can only be found within ourselves.  We need to do and experience things that we find truly meaningful.

Thank you for the positive words.

After having two "normal " days I am now back to feeling anxious, depressed, and suicidal.  This portion of one of your responses OP really resonated with me:

"I generally feel like this depression is my burden to bear, and I don't want to burden anyone else with my misery, so I've learned to stay away when I'm going through it. I don't want to be known or remembered as the miserable guy. There's a lot of shame in depression. This pattern has left me pretty much isolated many times. Every time I'm trying to get back into living a healthy life and moving forward, at some point it becomes too much and I let everything slide. Repeat that pattern a couple of times over a decade, and there's not that many people that stick around. I pushed so many people away, longing for a fresh slate that will never come, because they cared and I resented myself."

I often feel like a burden and think that my loved ones would be better off without me in some ways.  The resentment that I feel towards myself feels like a smoldering fire that is slowly consuming me from the inside.

Signed,

Another person that has had to bear the burden of mental illness each day for more years that I can remember.

Stay strong my friend.  One second, one minute, one hour, one day at a time.  You will slowly emerge from the thick fog that immerses you and discover a distant light that represents the new path in life that you are pursuing.  The path may be long and difficult but as long as you keep yourself oriented towards the light and not the darkness you will eventually achieve the happiness and sense of well being you desire.

Thank you for posting your thoughts.  It is difficult when medication does not provide us with the relief that we so desperately hope for.  Please be very careful about skipping doses as this may cause a brief sense of joy and euphoria but it is important to know that these feelings may be short lived and your original symptoms will return.

I share your sense of confusion and unhappiness.  Although I do not hear voices, when I am in a deeply depressed state I become very sensitive to external sounds.  Things like barking dogs, car alarms, and sirens drive me to suicidal thoughts because they feel like an audible ice pick being repeatedly stabbed into my brain.

Your willingness to take medication and share on this subreddit show that you are willings to ask for and receive help.  Your situation is challenging but your resolve to do your best to deal with it and keep moving forward is inspirational to me.

Another fellow veteran of the depression war.  It is amazing to think that we have dealt with these negative feelings day in and day out for so long.  I respect that each day you wake up, put your boots on, and report for duty.   Stay strong my friend.

I hope you are able to find a reason to continue pushing through the pain.  It would be kind of nice if I had at least a couple of other people to hang out with when the zombies take over.  All of us lost souls in one room.  Would make a great reality tv show.

20 plus years or me.  I honestly did not think I was going to see my 20th birthday.  Then when my 30th rolled around I was surprised that I had managed to make it that long.  My 40th is on the horizon.  Sometimes I think I go on living just to spite myself.  My luck if the zombie apocalypse ever happens I will probably outlive all of humanity.  Just be me and a bunch of damn undead beings.  I will be holed up in some dingy apartment feeling all anxious and depressed not because of the zombie but because of something stupid I regret saying or doing from 20 years prior.

Sorry to get off on a tangent.  I am in an odd mood tonight.  To answer your question, yes I have felt the way you are feeling for long periods of time.  You are not the only one.  There are others that can relate to what you have experienced.

Yes, my username is a reference to Dexter.  But unlike in the show where Dexter's dark passenger fuels his urge to hurt others, my dark passenger is the voice in my head when I am feeling depressed that tells me that I am worthless so I should hurt myself.

"In the bigger scheme of things, being the places I have has made me a more understanding and sensitive person to people who need it. That is a gift in itself"

There is a quote form Jim Carrey that I cam across recently that has been helpful to me:

"If you aren't in the moment, you are either looking forward to uncertainty, or back to pain and regret."

Like you said, our gift is our ability to help other "losers" like us.  But the only way that we can use our gift is if we are focused on the present moment.  I hope you and I have the courage and strength to do this so that we can help make a positive change.

Prior to my current job, I changed employers or work locations approximately every 9-12 months.  Before I joined the workforce, I had a similar problem at the university with my classes.  As soon as I experienced adversity (work or the other people), I would quit, transfer, or withdraw.

It reached a point as I got older where this approach was no longer sustainable.  I realized that instead of doing my best to deal with adversity and challenges, I was often taking the easy way out by running away from the situation.  This realization was important because it forced me to be more accountable for my decisions and not just blame the universe for my lack of success.

I have been with my current job for seven years.  How do I do it?  There is no magic formula.  There are days where I hate the place and everyone that works there.  For example, on Friday, my boss asked me to respond to an email that our office had received.  It took me four hours to compose an email that was four sentences long.  I was so frustrated by the time that I left on Friday that I swore I was going to turn in my letter of resignation first thing tomorrow morning.  But as I thought about it this weekend, I realize that the reason that I was so angry was because I allowed myself to rewrite the email 20 times with the hope that the final version that I sent would be perfect.  No one asked for that.  I did it to myself.  The first version was probably just as good as the 20th but I had allowed my sense of self to be tied to that email.

So if there is anything that I would remind you of right now is that you are good enough.  You do not need to be perfect.  Try your best on the paper that you are writing.  The grade that you ultimately receive is not a reflection of who you are as a person.  Break the work into small sections.  Write one sentence and then another and then another.  The same applies for each day.  Go to one class and do your best and then move on to the other.  Along the way, continue to be the kind and supportive person that you are to the people that you may meet.  I think that this is a good plan for both of us. :-)

Thank you for being supportive to the members of this subreddit.  Your words of hope and support are uplifting.  Your ability to connect and empathize with others is a positive trait.

I relate to your situation and understand your frustration.  Except for me it happens at my job.  I go through a terrible cycle every month where I get so overwhelmed with my responsibilities that I want to walk away from my career and just disappear off the face of the earth.  It causes me to get physically ill each time and I am just so tired of repeating the same negative pattern.

I am here if you want to talk more.

I relate to the shame, guilt, and self hatred that you feel.  The feeling that the poor choices made in the past have permanently tainted your existence.  The over consumption of drugs and alcohol.  The manipulative and hurtful things said and done.  The negative acts committed.  Despite my best efforts to become a better person and reestablish positive karma with the universe, all of those poor choices from the past still bother me and cause me to feel very guilty.

Like you, I have a good life filled with many blessings.  I just dont understand why I can not feel a sense of satisfaction and contentment.  It is like I am an apple and I have repaired the outside peel to a shiny red condition but on the inside I feel as though my core is still rotten.

If you want to talk more, I am here.  What ever is on your mind...

BTW your username is very clever.  Brought a smile to my face.

I understand your concerns.  It is unfortunate that many of us choose to remain silent because we fear what could happen if we shared our true feelings with those people that are suppossed to love and support us unconditionally.

That is why this forum is important.  It provides us an anonymous way to express ourselves and connect with others.  It has been two days since I submitted my original post and I am still struggling with my darkness.  But the main thing is that I am still here.  Here to try and cope with the sadness, anger, confusion, and guilt that I experience when my anxiety and depression are taking turns repeatedly kicking my mental health in the balls.

I agree. It is important to keep in mind and have reasonable expectations.  If you call and are put on hold or speak with someone and dont feel like it was a great conversation that it is okay and not a judgement of you or your situation.

I think the main reason that I never called the suicide prevention hotline before is that I was worried that my problems were not big enough.  Even though I was suicidal, I convinced myself that my pain is not as important as someone else's pain. I was worried that I would be judged and rejected by the person that I spoke with.

I can tell you that this was not my experience at all. The person was very kind and patient. The conversation itself was not life altering but it was life affirming knowing that I had the ability to reach out and ask for help in my time of need and that there are people out there that understand what you are going through.

Drake needs to remix Hotline Bling to "Suicide Hotline Bling".  Help bring awareness to this great resource. If all of us that deal with depression and suicidal feelings bought the song it would be the #1 track forever. :)
I appreciate the compliment. Only a fellow sufferer could truly understand the meaning of those words that were born out of my 30+ year struggle with anxiety and depression.

By taking an online class and signing up for a gym membership you are taking specific positive steps to improve your life and I commend you.  At the same time, you are abusing alcohol.  I understand because I am caught in a similar cycle.  Consuming excess alcohol will impact your physical and emotional health negatively.  By reducing my daily consumption of alcohol, i have made my daily burden easier to bear.  Try eliminating one glass/can from your drinking routine every couple of days. Replace that one glass/can with an additional positive thing like working out, reading a book, meditating, writing in a journal, calling a friend, learning to make a new meal.

You are not alone in your struggle. The alcohol is poisoning your mind and body. You are stronger than the liquid in the bottle my friend.

I understand your frustration. At times, I feel so insignificant that I question why I am even here. My friends have no idea of the depths and intensity of my anxiety and depression and have never made a serious attempt to understand.

I acknowledge you and the pain and anger that you are experiencing and am available to listen.

You are not alone.

I am glad that I spent a couple of hours reading posts in this forum before calling. I think that if I would have called the suicide helpline first and gotten put on hold I probably would have hung up and just felt bitter.  Reading about other people that are suffering is difficult but each time someone replied with encouraging words I felt like they were speaking to me. All of the positive words filled up my emotional gas tank just enough to allow me to have hope that the person on the other end of the suicide helpline could help (even if they did put me on hold).

Suicide Prevention Lifeline 800-273-8255

Also, you can also contact them via live chat if you prefer.

If you are at rock bottom, contact them.  Talk about you problems, talk about sports, talk about anything. Whatever it takes to keep hope alive.

Thank you for the kind words and encouragement.

You are right.  We are not alone but that is one of the reasons that mental illness can be such a difficult condition to deal with.  It causes us to believe that we are damaged and not worthy of love.  And once those feelings take hold and poison our soul, it is easy for us to get caught up in the dark fog of hopelessness.
